concept: The day is a before and after, so the hero greys out the morning (New Zealand 70 for 5) and puts the stumps score in bright white underneath it. Slide 2 splits the 243 into three bars: Nicholls and Phillips are two long bars and everyone else is one short one, so you see who made the day before reading a number. Slide 3 gives the unbroken 173 stand one giant figure, and slide 4 answers why with a single contrast in the headline (Bumrah 3 for 52, the rest 2 for 186) before asking who breaks the stand on day 2. Cricket blue, type and data only: no player photos, no logos.
caption:
New Zealand were 70 for 5. They finished day 1 on 243 for 5.

India chose to bowl at the Basin Reserve and Jasprit Bumrah made it count with 3 for 52. New Zealand were 60 for 4 at lunch and lost a fifth wicket at 70.

Then Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips batted out the day. Their unbroken stand is worth 173. Nicholls is 113 not out, his fifth Test hundred at the Basin Reserve. Phillips is 94 not out.

India's other bowlers took 2 for 186 between them. Nicholls was also dropped soon after his hundred when Devdutt Padikkal and Rishabh Pant both went for a top edge and neither held it.
